name: layered-progressive-disclosure
title: Layered Progressive Disclosure
description: A stack of inset rounded cards showing width and height readouts, a row whose label flips, and an asymmetric switch that reveals a two-tab selector and reverses the opacity and blur values. Each new layer springs in out of a blur.
use: Settings have levels of detail and advanced controls should stay hidden until switched on.
avoid: Reveals are click-only and the deep rounded nesting can read as busy in an already dense panel.
a11y: The feature row is a clickable div with no keyboard access, the switch has no aria-checked or label, and motion is never reduced. (keyboard: partial, labels: none, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A narrow dark panel titled Animation, built from rounded cards in shades of charcoal that sit one inside another. It holds two small stat chips, a wide label row with up-down chevrons, two value rows with an arrow between numbers, and a light Add Property button at the base.
behaves: Clicking the Visual Change row swaps its label to Transition and slides open an Asymmetric switch. Turning that switch on springs out a two-tab selector and flips the Opacity and Blur values, each layer appearing from above with a short blur.
customise: The title, two config rows, the feature, asymmetric and tab labels, and change callbacks are props; the nesting and grey shades are fixed in the file.
weight: light: A few nested panels with small layout and blur transitions that idle while closed.
demo: Width 320, Height 240, labels Visual Change and Transition, Asymmetric, and tabs Insertion and Removal.
issues: The Visual Change row is a div, so keyboard users cannot open the next layer.
The Asymmetric switch is a button with no aria-checked, role or label.
polishWhy: Neat nesting and gentle blur springs; missing switch semantics and keyboard access are real gaps.
